documents.generated_document: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 68-year-old male, established with this cardiology clinic, presenting with a 5-day history of progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea requiring 3 pillows, and a 10-pound weight gain. He has a known history of ischemic cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 25 percent, severe COPD, and stage 3b chronic kidney disease. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He reports strict adherence to his home Lasix 40 mg daily and fluid restrictions, but notes his urine output has decreased over the last 48 hours. PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: HFrEF, CAD s/p CABG, COPD, CKD stage 3b, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. MEDICATIONS: Furosemide 40 mg daily, Entresto 24/26 mg twice daily, Metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, Empagliflozin 10 mg daily, Albuterol inhaler PRN. REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Positive for dyspnea, orthopnea, lower extremity edema, and severe fatigue. Negative for fever, chills, chest pain, and syncope. PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Vitals: BP 105/65, HR 92, RR 22, SpO2 91 percent on room air. General: Mild respiratory distress, speaking in short sentences. Neck: JVP elevated to 12 cm H2O. Lungs: Bibasilar crackles extending halfway up the lung fields bilaterally. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, S3 gallop present, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema to the knees bilaterally, warm to touch. IMAGING AND LAB FINDINGS: BMP drawn yesterday at the primary care office shows BUN 45, Creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.5), Potassium 4.8. BNP is 1850 (baseline approx 600). Chest X-ray from yesterday demonstrates bilateral pleural effusions and prominent pulmonary vascular congestion. ASSESSMENT AND IMPRESSION: 1. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation, severe. 2. Acute kidney injury superimposed on CKD stage 3b, likely cardiorenal syndrome. PLAN AND FOLLOW-UP: The patient is at high risk for further decompensation. We had a lengthy discussion regarding direct admission to the hospital for IV diuresis versus aggressive outpatient management. The patient strongly prefers to avoid hospitalization if at all possible. We will attempt outpatient management with very close monitoring. Administered IV Furosemide 80 mg in the clinic today. Will increase home Furosemide to 80 mg twice daily. Holding Entresto temporarily given the acute kidney injury. Strict fluid restriction of less than 1.5 liters per day and daily morning weights. Ordered stat BMP and BNP to be drawn in 48 hours to monitor renal function and electrolytes on the higher diuretic dose. The patient is scheduled for a follow-up visit in this clinic in exactly 2 days. Explicit return precautions given; instructed to go to the nearest emergency department immediately if respiratory distress worsens or if he develops chest pain.
documents.Justification: The CPT code 99215 is supported by a High level of Medical Decision Making (MDM) for an established patient. The number and complexity of problems addressed is High, as the patient presents with a severe exacerbation of a chronic illness (acute on chronic systolic heart failure) and an acute illness posing a threat to bodily function (acute kidney injury/cardiorenal syndrome). The amount and complexity of data reviewed is Moderate (reviewing external labs and imaging). The risk of complications and morbidity is High due to the decision to initiate aggressive IV and high-dose oral diuretic therapy in the setting of acute kidney injury, which requires intensive monitoring for toxicity (stat labs in 48 hours, close follow-up), as well as the explicit consideration and discussion of hospital admission. Meeting two of the three MDM elements (Problems and Risk) at the High level qualifies the encounter for 99215.
